Corporate.brandNameRationale: Two words. Bayfield is a real place name with a quiet weight; it sounds like the headquarters of a firm that has been around. Software closes it plainly. The pair avoids the 'Platform Group' and 'Systems Partners' templates and reads as a real, established enterprise software firm.
Corporate.industrySummary: Mid-market enterprise software is dominated by the giant legacy vendors at the top and a long tail of point solutions at the bottom. The opening is for a structured mid-size firm focused on the operator-grade product work.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Workday (workday.com) holds the enterprise platform peer position. ServiceNow (servicenow.com) sits at the institutional tier. Procore (procore.com) does the vertical-specific middle. Atlassian (atlassian.com) holds the developer-team peer. We sit smaller, focused on the operator middle.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Enterprise software for mid-market operators that have outgrown spreadsheets and aren't ready for Workday.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Mid-market operators are too small for the giants' attention and too sophisticated for point solutions. We sit between them with operating depth and modern usability.

Corporate.tagline: Enterprise workflow software for regulated industries.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Lattimer is a surname pulled from a 1960s engineering firm that built control systems. Systems Group is the category. The pair signals a serious vendor — the kind a procurement team enters into a master agreement with, not a tool a developer signs up to with a credit card.
Corporate.manifesto: We build software for the part of the enterprise where downtime has a number attached. The buyer is a director of operations, not a head of growth. The contract is three years, not three months. We ship slowly and predictably because the customer's calendar runs on slow, predictable cycles.
Corporate.industrySummary: Regulated industries — healthcare, financial services, energy, defense — are mid-cycle on a workflow software refresh. The legacy vendors are tired. The cloud-native vendors are not enterprise-ready. The opening is for a serious, deliberate mid-vendor with the discipline of the incumbents and the architecture of the cloud-native cohort.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: ServiceNow (servicenow.com) is the incumbent. Pegasystems (pega.com) holds the workflow-platform middle. Appian (appian.com) is the modern alternative. We sit underneath them, narrower and deeper, focused only on regulated workflow.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Lattimer Systems Group provides workflow software for regulated industries — built for audit, change-control, and procurement realities.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Our differentiator is the parts of enterprise software the customer never sees in a demo: audit trails, role separation, environment promotion, vendor security review. We ship those first and the workflow surface second.

Corporate.brandDescription: Bramley Software Group operates a portfolio of B2B SaaS brands across vertical software, infrastructure, and business operations categories.
Corporate.scope:
Bramley Software Group works across:
• Multi-brand B2B SaaS operations
• Shared enterprise sales and account management
• Shared platform engineering and SRE function
• Cross-portfolio compliance (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP)
• Annual investor and operator reporting
Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier B2B SaaS brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: A SaaS operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the enterprise sales and platform operations are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — enterprise sales runs on schedule.
Reliable — predictable terms across the portfolio.
Discreet — brand relationships stay between us and the brand.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Bramley is a real English place-name with a heritage trade register. Software Group follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in B2B SaaS (Vista Equity Partners' platform structure, Thoma Bravo's portfolio structure, Insight Partners' approach). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Bramley Software Group owns and operates a portfolio of B2B SaaS brands. Each brand retains its identity, engineering team, and product roadmap; we operate the shared enterprise sales infrastructure, compliance, and back office. The buyer is a brand founder considering sale, an enterprise consolidating SaaS vendor relationships, or an institutional investor holding SaaS assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: B2B SaaS has consolidated under a small number of multi-brand platforms (Vista Equity Partners portfolio, Thoma Bravo portfolio, Insight Partners). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep enterprise sales operations and the procurement-grade reliability enterprise SaaS customers require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Vista Equity Partners (vistaequitypartners.com) is the multi-brand SaaS reference. Thoma Bravo (thomabravo.com) holds the multi-brand peer slot. Insight Partners (insightpartners.com) sits in the multi-brand peer position. Constellation Software (csisoftware.com) plays the heritage multi-brand SaaS peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand SaaS operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Bramley Software Group is a regional multi-brand B2B SaaS operator running enterprise sales, compliance, and shared platform operations across a portfolio of independent product brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared enterprise sales infrastructure, compliance reach, and the operational reliability brand founders need without giving up engineering direction.

Creative.tagline: Software for the part of the work that isn't shipping.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Modulo is the mathematical operator for the remainder after division — single uncommon technical word. Software is the plain category suffix.
Creative.manifesto: Most software brands sell perfection: the seamless workflow, the zero-bug release, the magical transformation. We made Off By One because the actual experience of software is debugging the small mistake nobody caught. The brand is for the engineers who know that the work is mostly in the corrections, the version increments, the patches that nobody announces.
Creative.industrySummary: SaaS branding has been polished, transformation-led, and slightly anxious. There's room for a brand that's warm, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about the actual quiet work of building good software.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Linear (linear.app) holds the design-led restraint peer. Vercel (vercel.com) sits at the modern monochrome tier. Cursor (cursor.com) does the modern dev-tool middle. Tailscale (tailscale.com) holds the warm-technical peer. We sit warmer than all of them, with a clearer point of view.
Creative.positioningStatement: A SaaS brand for engineers who know the work is mostly in the corrections.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Engineers, engineering managers, technical founders. Already use four SaaS tools. Pick tools based on whether the brand feels like the team that built it would actually use it.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Margin is the real word for the space outside the main column — and the real word for the time outside main production. As a software brand name it stakes a position on the non-output parts of work.
Creative.manifesto: Every software company markets the same way: we are fast, we are getting faster, we are using AI to be even faster. We started Slow Software because the work we want to do — and the work our customers want to do — is not actually faster when the tool is faster. The work is slower. The tool should match.
Creative.industrySummary: Productivity software has confused speed with quality. The customer who notices the difference is rare, but real, and currently underserved. There is room for a brand that takes the opposite side of every SaaS argument and treats slowness as a feature.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Cortado (cortado.app), Daylight (daylightcomputer.com), and the Reflect (reflect.app) cohort touch the slow-tech edge. We are louder and more opinionated than any of them — the name is the position.
Creative.positioningStatement: Slow Software is a workshop building deliberately slow productivity tools — for people who think the speed is the problem.
Creative.positioningRationale: We make the case for slowness explicit in everything: the name, the manifesto, the release cadence, the support hours. Customers self-select.

motivations: Want a tool that is on their side, not the platform's.

dos: Argue the slow case explicitly in copy.

Email customers a quarterly letter, not a weekly digest.
Refuse to comp the holidays with a sale.
donts: No livechat support — write longer emails instead.

Creative.tagline: A SaaS company for the part of the work between commits.
Creative.brandDescription: The Build Step Co is a creative-led SaaS company building tools and observability for the build step — the transformation between source code and deployable artifacts that most engineering teams treat as an afterthought.
Creative.scope:
The Build Step Co works across:
• Build observability and metrics across CI/CD pipelines
• Build-step optimization tooling (cache management, dependency analysis)
• Quarterly published essays on the build-step tradition
• Open-source tooling for build observability
• Educational programs for build engineers
Creative.mission: To treat the build step as a first-class engineering discipline.
Creative.vision: A SaaS company whose build-step observability becomes a standard reference for serious engineering teams.
coreValues: Specific — every build step is observable.
Considered — the build step is a discipline.
Warm — the workspace respects the engineer.
Literary — the writing about builds is part of the work.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Build Step is the universally-understood engineering trade phrase for the transformation between source code and deployable artifacts — the CI/CD compile-and-package phase. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school. Stands in the lineage of declarative engineering-tooling brands.
Creative.manifesto: Most engineering tooling treats the build step as a black box. We started The Build Step Co because the actual most-watched-but-least-instrumented part of the engineering lifecycle is the build. We instrument it, optimize it, and write about it as a first-class engineering discipline.
Creative.industrySummary: Engineering tooling has matured around source-code and observability layers. The opening is for a creative-led company that explicitly positions on the build step — the layer between source and runtime — as its primary creative position.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Earthly (earthly.dev) plays the closest peer in build tooling. Buildkite (buildkite.com) holds the CI/CD peer slot. Garden (garden.io) sits in the build-and-deploy peer position. CircleCI (circleci.com) plays the CI/CD platform peer reference. We sit alongside Earthly with a sharper build-step observability focus.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Build Step Co is a SaaS company building tools and observability for the CI/CD build step as a first-class engineering discipline.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the build-step position. Every tool, every essay, and every open-source contribution is built around the build step.

behaviors: Maintain CI/CD pipelines across multiple repositories.
Care about build times, cache hit rates, and pipeline reliability.
Read engineering blogs about build infrastructure.
Subscribe to engineering newsletters.
motivations: Want tools that treat the build step as serious work.
Want a workspace built for build optimization.
Want observability built specifically for builds.

dos: Publish the quarterly essay on the build-step tradition.
Reference specific build patterns by name.
Show actual build observability data in marketing.
Sign release notes by the engineer who shipped the feature.

messagingPillars.description: Observability and metrics for the build step — build times, cache hit rates, dependency analysis, pipeline reliability — as the primary product.
